requestSummary: Upgrade Jessy Graph to V2 so it turns the subagent deviations observed in the jessy-skills-only session into deterministic runtime controls, while explicitly routing worker-safe jessy-skills for implementation and code-quality guidance.
approvedInScope: Add a real plan-only and execution-resume task protocol
Disable built-in worker multi-agent delegation and deny recursive Codex execution through worker commands
Validate task changes against the immutable task base, including worker-created commits
Add explicit task roles, required skill routing, immutable skill snapshots, and deterministic code-quality profiles
Run verification and review through clean or read-only execution contexts that workers cannot weaken
Convert the audited T7 and T8 deviation patterns into V2 regression and live acceptance cases
Preserve host-native MCP operation, five-process scheduling, durable recovery, and serial integration
Route all planners and semantic reviewers to gpt-5.6-luna, and all implementers and repair workers to deepseek-v4-flash
approvedOutOfScope: Automatic merge into operator repositories, push, deployment, or migration
Replacing jessy-skills semantic planning with autonomous Jessy Graph planning
Treating JSONL monitoring or worker self-reports as the primary security authority
preservedDecisions: Authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP on 0.0.0.0:8003 for localhost and trusted LAN use
Project-local runtime data and service configuration
Reuse of host /root/.codex configuration and authentication
At most five conflict-free workers and serial integration
all task planners use gpt-5.6-luna regardless of complexity
all per-task and final combined reviewers use gpt-5.6-luna
all implementers and repair workers use deepseek-v4-flash; deepseek-v4-pro is forbidden
No automatic write-back to operator source repositories
sourceEvidence: The audited session used jessy-skills directly rather than Jessy Graph and supplies threat-model cases, not Jessy Graph failure evidence
Codex CLI 0.145.0 supports read-only and workspace-write sandboxes, exact-session resume, JSONL events, and a per-process multi_agent feature override
Official Codex source evidence shows built-in subagents are in-process and shell commands can still start a separate Codex process
Current Jessy Graph workers discover the global skill catalog but do not select, snapshot, or require specific skills
Current Git boundary checks inspect working-tree status relative to current HEAD and do not reject worker-created commits
constraints: Keep project-workflow-codex in the main Codex session rather than inside bounded workers
Use only worker-safe execution and domain skills selected by the approved task contract
Do not rely on prompts alone for delegation, command, file, plan, or evidence boundaries
Do not use --strict-config, --output-schema, --ignore-user-config, danger-full-access, or sandbox bypass
Keep credentials and worker-control policies outside target task worktrees
Preserve all unrelated user changes in both repositories
Do not preserve or migrate V1 runtime state because Jessy Graph has never carried user data
